name: Melted or Drawn Butter, No. 3
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Wet the flour to a smooth paste with a little cold milk, and add to the hot water in the inner vessel, stirring until thick.
Have ready the beaten egg in a cup.
Take a teaspoonful of the mixture from the fire, and beat with this until light; then another, and still another.
Set aside the cup when this is done, and stir the butter into the contents of the inner saucepan gradually, until thoroughly mixed, then add the beaten egg in the same way.

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Wet the flour to a smooth paste with a little cold milk, and add to the hot water in the inner vessel, stirring until thick.
2. Have ready the beaten egg in a cup.
3. Take a teaspoonful of the mixture from the fire, and beat with this until light; then another, and still another.
4. Set aside the cup when this is done, and stir the butter into the contents of the inner saucepan gradually, until thoroughly mixed, then add the beaten egg in the same way.
